Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The Flote is described as a wind instrument designed for people with limited mobility, emphasizing accessibility, calibration to users’ physical abilities, low cost, and ease of fabrication. The focus is on creating an accessible, expressive musical instrument and even as a form of physical therapy, indicating a primary utilitarian/assistive goal with enjoyment and creative expression layered on. There is no mention of co-design workshops with disabled or diverse stakeholders, nor of repurposing an entertainment game. This aligns best with a mostly utility-first design where the primary utilitarian mechanic (accessible musical control via head movement and breath) is designed first, with fun and creativity incorporated but not as the originating driver.

        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: Participants freely explored the instrument by moving their heads and reacting to the sounds, with no mention of explicit rules, goals, or game structure; this aligns with unstructured creative play rather than a game or structured activity.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The Flote is a musical instrument where outcomes (notes, pitch, volume) are directly and deterministically controlled by the user’s head movement and breath, with calibration to match abilities. There is no mention of randomness or chance elements; performance is entirely based on user skill and control, so it is entirely skill-based.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),
        (5) entirely social (i.e., tag)
reasoning: The Flote is described as a musical instrument controlled by an individual user’s head movement and breath, with calibration and interaction focused on a single player. User testing is discussed in terms of individuals learning and composing, with no mention of multiplayer, collaboration, or social play features. This aligns with an entirely solo design.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The Flote is a single-player musical instrument where sound is produced continuously based on real-time head movement and breath, without any notion of discrete turns, steps, or phases. Actions (movement and blowing) occur continuously and simultaneously, matching the definition of an entirely simultaneous system.

        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),

reasoning: The Flote is a musical instrument controlled by real-time head movement and breath, explicitly contrasted with non-realtime composition tools; interaction and sound production are continuous and immediate, indicating an entirely synchronous design rather than involving asynchronous affordances.

        (1) entirely competitive (i.e., spit card game),
        (2) mostly competitive, but sometimes collaboration is important (i.e., forbidden island),
        (3) mix of competitive and collaborative (i.e., mario party 2 vs 2 mini-games),
        (4) mostly collaborative (i.e., animal crossing),
        (5) entirely collaborative (i.e., pandemic)
reasoning: The Flote is a single-user expressive musical instrument and therapy tool, with no mention of competition, scoring, or adversarial mechanics. Its purpose is creative expression and accessibility, which aligns with an entirely collaborative/non-competitive design rather than any competitive or mixed mode.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The Flote is a single-player musical instrument with no roles or differing mechanics between players; everyone uses the same headset, breath, and head-movement mapping (calibrated per user but functionally identical). This corresponds to an entirely symmetrical design rather than asymmetrical roles or abilities.
